title: Rigveda 5.70: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.70: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.70 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 387v-388r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.70.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 387v
translation.original_text:
1pu̱rū̱ruṇā̍ ci̱d dhy asty avo̍ nū̱naṁ vā̍ṁ varuṇa | mitra̱ vaṁsi̍ vāṁ suma̱tim ||
2tā vā̍ṁ sa̱myag a̍druhvā̱ṇeṣa̍m aśyāma̱ dhāya̍se | va̱yaṁ te ru̍drā syāma ||
translation.text:
1EVEN far and wide, O Varuṇa and Mitra, doth your grace extend. May I obtain your kind good-will.
2From you, benignant Gods, may we gain fully food for sustenance. Such, O ye Rudras, my we be.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 387v (numbered 60v by the scribe) (OPenn image 388, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.69.2 ‹-tisṝṇām dhiṣaṇānām retaḥ-dhāḥ vi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 388r (numbered 61r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.70.3 ‹tanū-bhiḥ›. Verses 5.70.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1puru-uruṇā | cit | hi | asti | avaḥ | nūnam | vām | varuṇa | mitra | vaṃsi | vām | su-matim
2tā | vām | samyak | adruhvāṇā | iṣam | aśyāma | dhāyase | vayam | te | rudrā | syāma

translation.original_ref: RV 5.70.3-4 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 388r
translation.original_text:
3pā̱taṁ no̍ rudrā pā̱yubhi̍r u̱ta trā̍yethāṁ sutrā̱trā | tu̱ryāma̱ dasyū̍n ta̱nūbhi̍ḥ ||
4mā kasyā̍dbhutakratū ya̱kṣam bhu̍jemā ta̱nūbhi̍ḥ | mā śeṣa̍sā̱ mā tana̍sā ||
translation.text:
3Guard us, O Rudras. with your guar4 save us, ye skilled to save, my we Subdue the Dasyus, we ourselves,
4Or ne'er may we, O Wondrous Strong, enjoy another's solemn feast, Ourselves, our sons, or progeny.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 388r (numbered 61r by the scribe) (OPenn image 388, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.70.3 ‹tanū-bhiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 388v (numbered 61v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.73.1 ‹yat adya sthaḥ pārāvati›. Verses 5.70.3-4 end on this page; 5.70.3 begins on fol. 387v (numbered 60v by the scribe).

3pātam | naḥ | rudrā | pāyu-bhiḥ | uta | trāyethām | su-trātrā | turyāma | dasyūn | tanū-bhiḥ
4mā | kasya | adbhutakratūity adbhuta-kratū | yakṣam | bhujema | tanūbhiḥ | mā | śeṣasā | mā | tanasā
